I have been playing Tower Unite for many years now, and just got to 500 hours in, so I decided to finally review it. 

Tower Unite is a game consisting of multiple smaller games within, spanning multiple genres. There is Mini golf, a few FPS games, ball race (think monkey ball or marble games), a online hub world with an arcade, casino, stores, boardwalk games and even a few rides to enjoy as well as a waterpark! Though my favorite is this on rails shooting dark ride called "Dark Voyage". I really love those rides IRL and this is no exception! There are even homes you can buy (called Condos) and you can decorate them however you want like a 3D Animal Crossing. Other games and things to do are scattered around the Hub, or Plaza, as well, though some do require multiple people do play them which can be a problem sometimes. 

I do particularity enjoy the seasonal events they do every so often, Halloween, Christmas, Anniversary event, Easter, and Summer! Each let you earn coins by playing which can be spent to earn anything in the shop,including stuff from past years, eliminating FOMO which I love to see. The events usually run around a month, and sometimes a bit longer in a few cases. 

I have been playing this game for awhile, as I said. Updates can be a bit slow feeling sometimes, the small team is always working on new stuff, though if you are a fan of a certain feature or game mode, you might be waiting a bit, though this is only because the team is working on other game modes and such in the meantime. Overall, improvements have been made for a much smoother gameplay experience, which is a huge help! I personally do not always like some of the changes made, but overall I'd certainly say they are positive. 

The game is more of a "Hangout and Vibe" game than anything, you basically make your own experience and play what you like, with something for everyone. I usually always find myself coming back to it as a nice comfort game. 

Even though it may say "Early Access" the game is complete and quite playable. The team seems ready to launch the game soon, though I wouldn't let that stop anyone from giving it a try. For $20 normal it is a very good deal for what you get. Alone or with others it is a great game that deserves more recognition!

192478828.review:
So, I got [i]Tower Unite[/i] back when it released, which was apparently way back in 2016. Wow does the time fly. Meaning I've owned this game for about nine years now, give or take, though I will admit, I stopped playing maybe back in 2019ish? So, I was eager to jump back into the game to see what had changed during those last six years. The answer? Mini game wise, it feels like an archived version of one of those old websites I used to play on, aka preserved exactly how I remember it, which isn't what you want to hear about an early access title. There's no polish here, it's just as clunky as it ever was, and with most of the early player base supporting it [i]because[/i] we were led to believe we'd eventually see that polish, this is extremely disappointing. Everything is as amateur in execution as it was from the beginning, and none of what was treated as "skeletons" for better mini games to come have actually been improved on. Literally, if you wanted to know what it was like to play this game back when I was super into it years ago, all you'd need to do is buy a copy and play it now. Well, almost.

Because here's the real kicker, some of the features seem to actually work less now than when I last played the game, something you [b]absolutely[/b] do not want to hear about an early access game. The character customization is the most notable. It is completely broken, especially when it comes to workshop models, absolutely refusing to save the one you've selected, which is unfortunate because the default avatars are...let's just say not good. Those, however, were broken too. The game kept struggling to save or display my avatar's hair and eye color even for the default model, which just kept showing up white. In a game about community, one of the last things you want to stop working is your avatar customization. Side note, I was one of the individuals worried the game introducing modding for avatars would be used as an excuse to not improve on the default ones. Here we are years later, and the avatars have not only gone untouched, they're worse. In general, the game really struggled to load the images of items, which caused me to just stare at blank gray blocks for some of them. I was shocked as I didn't remember this being an issue, and if it was, it should have been fixed by now.

The mini games, again, are just as clunky as ever and feel weird to play if you've ever played more fleshed out versions of them (the mini games are quite basic, so you most likely have). Which was fine back in the early days, the creators were finding their footing and developing each as they went, but not after nine years of early access. I honestly should have taken it as a warning sign when they kept adding new mini games, instead of working on the ones they already had, which it felt like so many players were desperately asking them to. I was almost going to write into my review that mini golf was the only worth while mini game, but I found even that isn't true, as a lot of the courses feel designed to be annoying to play, and also go on for [i]way[/i] too long. There's difficulty, and then there's just throwing as many corners and walls into my path as possible to the point it becomes tedious. Some courses have cool themes, but, within them, each level felt way too similar to really grab my attention. I'd originally planned to try and play all the courses when it was the only mini game I still actually enjoyed, but I soon found myself way too bored to bother. And no, playing it with friends wouldn't help, as the courses in and of themselves just aren't fun. So, after years of development, I have a multiplayer game stuck in my library I would never choose to play with anyone, even if they happened to have it.

The only thing that is still the same, in a good way, is the condos. I need people who haven't played this game to understand playing around and decorating the condos is so fun, that I legit think if these creators just made a condo building game with fun house designs and the ability to use workshop avatars as models, people would go crazy over it. Ensuring there's just the right amount of customization options for the furniture items and a good variety of designs for the condos is clearly where these creators excel. The layouts for the mini games? Weird combined with clunky controls that makes them annoying to sit through. The layouts for the condos? Extremely nice to work with decoration wise or unique in a super fun way. There is a literal underwater condo with an animated airlock so you can go swim out in the ocean! I felt way more achieved getting the achievement for discovering that after all these years than trying to sit through golf. It's enough to be fun without being too under or overwhelming. The most fun this game has ever truly given me is just goofing off as my favorite characters in the condos, along with decorating them. If this feature ever gets broken, I will legit be so heart broken, as I will definitely visit them again in the future. This is the only reason this game is still in my Steam library. 

Yet, with all of that in mind, I just absolutely can not recommend new players spend any money on this, even if they know a friend who owns it. There are so many better multiplayer and party games out there at this point that cover the mini games [i]Tower Unite[/i] tried to implement, that this game kind of just can't compete with them anymore. This game really fell short by not being able to actually polish any its features. As I said above, almost everything feels as rushed and shallow as when the game first came out, which is not a good sign. The fact levels were still coming out for mini games back then, yet there's really nothing of note in all this time shocks me. I think a lot of the modern multiplayer and party games out now are great examples of how to succeed. Don't spread yourself too thin, focus on one overarching mechanic or gameplay loop and be really good at it. [i]Tower Unite[/i] wanted to be every party game in one, but ultimately failed. Well, unless we count the condos, but as fun as the condos are, it's not worth buying a game that seems to be eternally stuck in early access Hell just for them. [i]Tower Unite[/i] feels haunted with potential, but it's become clear we'll likely never reach the finish line with this one.

I like this game, it has a lot of promise and I really want to give it a good review, but based on it's current state and the course of development so far, I simply can't in good conscience recommend this game.

So for those of you who don't know, Tower Unite was intended to be a standalone version and expansion of GMod Tower. It was supposed to be a bunch of different games and activities all bundled together within a virtual world that you could play in. It originally started as a pitch on Kickstarter and Indiegogo and evolved from there. In general, it is a good concept that could lead to an amazing game, however, there are several issues that hinder it.

The first and most obvious issue is that progress is slow... [i]REALLY SLOW.[/i] The game has been in early access for 8 years now and many of the things promised in the original kickstarter and indiegogo campaigns were either just recently added or haven't been added yet. It took them over 4 years to add the nightclub and billiards they promised in the original funding campaign, It took them until February of 2021 to add SDNL, something that was once again promised in the original campaign. It took them until just a couple months ago to finally partially add the boardwalk games and bumper cars that were promised in the original campaign. Plenty of things promised in the original campaign such as Panic at Horror Hill, air hockey, the shooting gallery, condo pets, and cooking still aren't in the game and aren't slated to be in the game for at least a couple more years. Based on the current and historic rate of development and the number of items left on the trello, TU likely won't exit EA any earlier than 2028, [i]12 years after entering early access.[/i]

The second biggest issue is of course the questionable development schedule and choices made by the devs. The dev team has consistently made confusing and sometimes downright questionable choices in development, like working on reworks for existing systems prior to working on the content that was promised in the original campaign. As was stated in the previous part, many of the original promises from the campaign have been moved to the backlog on the development Trello and have no estimated timeframe for when they will be released. Instead, Pixeltail is spending their time working on changes and reworks of already existing content, stuff that should reasonably be put on the backburner until the game is feature complete.

Additionally, as someone who has ADHD, the development of this game can best be described as unmedicated ADHD, with the devs working on one component for a bit only to shelve it to go work on another component, only to shelve that one to go work on another one. A perfect example of this is the boardwalk shooting gallery, which was almost entirely done with development back in April od 2021, yet it was shelved and hasn’t been touched since, with the devs instead focusing on other things that were much farther from being complete. As someone who has ADHD, this way of working on a project simply never gets things done in any reasonable amount of time. Another example of this is the Pixel Crusaders: Phase One achievement. This is an achievement that was added to the game 4 years ago which requires you to earn at least 15 tickets in every game included in Arcade Phase One in one sitting. Arcade Phase One was added to the game back in April of 2020, meaning that everything needed to earn this achievement has been in the game for [i]OVER 4 YEARS[/i], despite that, still to this day the achievement is impossible to get because Pixeltail still hasn’t added the functionality to earn it, something that would take very little effort to do.

Then there is of course all the little things that really bother me. The fact that pixeltail regularly makes a habit of adding achievements long before you can earn them. This includes the Pixel Crusader achievement above, but also an achievement for cooking a meal (cooking has not yet been implemented and has no planned date for release) as well as achievements for RC Race and Battle Boats, which have both also not be added yet. 

Additionally, there are many games and activities that were added to the game months to years ago that still do not have trophies, milestone items or both including SDNL, Accelerate, Dark Voyage, Boardwalk, Nightclub, Condos and Halloween, as well as several activities that are very lacking in milestone items such as Casino, Trivia and Typing Derby. Virus is really wonky and is one of the few activities that actually could use a rework yet it seems to be the only one not getting a rework.

And then finally there are the copious amounts of in-game achievements that are simply designed to be annoying grindfests solely to increase playtime, they aren’t difficult, they just take ridiculous amounts of time. These include the achievements for jumping 200k times in plaza, watching [i]10 WHOLE HOURS[/i] of TV in a condo, playing every one of the 13 ball race maps 30 times each (you’ll have completed all the other achievements for them and start to get bored of them around 10-12 playthoughs each), having to play every accelerate map 20 times, having to play a full round of every one of the 13 minigolf map 10 times each (join in progress doesn’t count, you have to start from hole 1 and you’ll probably have gotten all the holes in one by your 4th playthrough), watching theater for 2 hours, or surviving 25 times on each of the 7 Virus maps, which takes a [i]minimum[/i] of 25 rounds on each if you somehow manage to survive every single time, which you won’t.

So TL:DR, an excellent concept marred by extremely slow development, questionable development choices and a borderline ADHD dev team that can’t actually decide what to work on.
